title: Not All Neighbors Matter: Understanding the Impact of Graph Sparsification on GNN Pipelines
abstract: arXiv:2603.06952v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: As graphs scale to billions of nodes and edges, graph Machine Learning workloads are constrained by the cost of multi-hop traversals over exponentially growing neighborhoods. While various system-level and algorithmic optimizations have been proposed to accelerate Graph Neural Network (GNN) pipelines, data management and movement remain the primary bottlenecks at scale. In this paper, we explore whether graph sparsification, a well-established technique that reduces edges to create sparser neighborhoods, can serve as a lightweight pre-processing step to address these bottlenecks while preserving accuracy on node classification tasks.   We develop an extensible experimental framework that enables systematic evaluation of how different sparsification methods affect the performance and accuracy of GNN models. We conduct the first comprehensive study of GNN training and inference on sparsified graphs, revealing several key findings. Firs

tldr: 本文首次系统研究了图稀疏化作为预处理步骤对GNN流水线的影响，发现并非所有邻居都同等重要，并提出了可扩展实验框架以评估不同稀疏化方法在保持节点分类准确性的同时缓解大规模图计算瓶颈的效果。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first comprehensive study on graph sparsification as a preprocessing step for GNN pipelines, revealing that not all neighbors are equally important and proposing an extensible framework to evaluate sparsification methods for mitigating scalability bottlenecks while preserving node classification accuracy.
